column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
How can we learn about people who lived long before anyone could write, and how much of the human story does that cover?
What is the difference between humans changing in body and humans changing in how they live, and what did producing surplus make possible?
Which early human ancestor first left Africa, roughly when, and which later wave carried our own species out?
What kinds of evidence do archaeologists dig up, and how do the tools of the 'handy man', the upright walker and our own species compare?
On what basis do historians divide the distant past into ages, and what are the three stages of the Stone Age?
Name two early Indian sites and say what the big stone tools found there were used for.
How did tools and expressions of ideas change as hunters became more skilled?
What changed in the world when the climate warmed after the last ice age and how did that affect human numbers?
What tools and foods marked everyday Mesolithic life, and where can we still see their paintings?
What knowledge helped hunters begin to grow their own food, and what was the core change they made to plants and animals?
How did a farmer's toolkit and home differ from a hunter-gatherer's, and was this change worldwide at one time?
Describe the first farming village of the subcontinent: where it was, roughly when, and how its people lived.
What new material did the people of Mehrgarh start to work, and what great civilisation grew from it?
What difference did the first metal tools make to farming communities in the Indus region?
Which crafts and which features of settlements show that the Harappan culture grew from earlier communities rather than appearing suddenly?
Why would standard weights matter for trade, and what two developments led from the early stage to cities?
Name the four river-valley civilisations and the rivers they grew by, and say which two traded most closely and why.
What did the Sumerians pioneer in irrigation, building, religion and writing, and what shaped the way their cities were organised?
Which later Mesopotamian rulers and states followed the Sumerians, and what lasting contribution did the Babylonian king make?
How did the yearly flooding of a river lead Egyptians to farming advances, a way of tracking time and the beginnings of government?
What did the Egyptians believe happened to a person after death, and how did that belief shape what they built and did with the dead?
How was the lost script of ancient Egypt finally read, and what helped the scholar who did it?
Which rivers fed early Chinese civilisation and how did it move from Neolithic villages to cities and dynasties?
What is the oldest evidence about China, and which products and institutions made China famous in the ancient world?
